lines.en: Finally, in 1941, lawmakers in Congress made the fourth Thursday in November a legal holiday.
lines.zh: 终于，在 1941 年，国会议员把 11 月的第四个星期四定为法定假日。

lines.en: This Thanksgiving, millions of Americans will gather to eat a meal and express their thanks. Their gatherings may echo George Washington's first Thanksgiving proclamation. In it, the first president made a point of declaring that people of all religions should celebrate Thanksgiving.
lines.zh: 今年感恩节，数百万美国人将聚在一起吃饭、表达感谢。他们的聚会也许呼应着乔治·华盛顿的第一份感恩节公告。在公告中，这位首任总统特别宣布，所有宗教的人都应该庆祝感恩节。

lines.en: That idea is still important. Almost everyone in the country, including immigrants, observes the holiday in some way.
lines.zh: 这个理念至今仍然重要。这个国家几乎每个人，包括移民，都以某种方式过这个节。

lines.en: Kirkpatrick says that for new Americans, the day can be a rite of passage. In her words, "The idea is that once you celebrate Thanksgiving, you know you are truly participating in a national festival that cements your position as an American."
lines.zh: 柯克帕特里克说，对新美国人来说，这一天可以是一种“成人礼”。用她的话说：“这个理念就是，一旦你过了感恩节，你就知道自己真正参与了一个全国性的节日，这巩固了你作为美国人的身份。”

qs.q: Why did some lawmakers object to a national Thanksgiving?
opts: They saw it as religious and a power of the states.
qs.a: They saw it as religious and a power of the states.
qs.why: "Critics had two main concerns."

qs.q: What did Washington do to satisfy opponents?
opts: He asked each state leader to call the holiday.
qs.a: He asked each state leader to call the holiday.
qs.why: "He asked them to call a national Thanksgiving on the day he had chosen."

qs.q: When did Thanksgiving become a legal holiday?
qs.why: "Finally, in 1941..."

gloss: 成人礼；（人生）重要的过渡仪式

lessons.title: Old Clothing Gains New Popularity at Vintage Stores
lessons.zh: 古着店里的旧衣新潮
lessons.sum: 越来越多美国人去古着店买旧衣服：省钱、环保又有个性。时尚业排放约占全球温室气体的 10%，李维斯等大品牌也开始回收旧牛仔裤。对年轻人来说，旧 T 恤还带着一份怀旧。

lines.en: Americans in greater numbers are buying used clothing.
lines.zh: 越来越多的美国人在买二手衣服。

lines.en: Fans call it vintage clothing. They believe buying old, used clothes can save money. They also consider it good for the environment and stylish. Vintage stores sell clothes from previous time periods. The stores often carry famous brands and sell them at low prices.
lines.zh: 喜欢它的人称之为“古着”（vintage clothing）。他们认为买旧衣服能省钱，还觉得这样环保又时髦。古着店卖的是过去年代的衣服，常常有名牌，价格却很低。

lines.en: Vintage clothing has been on the rise for about 10 years. It is driven largely by a new generation of people who are concerned about sustainable ways of living. That means they want to waste less and use natural resources carefully.
lines.zh: 古着流行起来已经有大约 10 年了，主要推动力是关心可持续生活方式的新一代人。也就是说，他们想少浪费，并谨慎使用自然资源。

lines.en: In 2018, the United Nations said that the fashion industry causes "around 10% of global greenhouse gas emissions." The U.N. said the industry uses more energy than the airplane and shipping industries combined.
lines.zh: 2018 年，联合国说，时尚业造成了“全球约 10% 的温室气体排放”。联合国说，这个行业消耗的能源比航空业和航运业加起来还多。

lines.en: Jen Mason is the owner of Underground Vintage in Lewes, Delaware, a town on the Atlantic coast. She said that clothes in the store that do not get sold are provided to local people. They use the material for different purposes such as making blankets. Unsold clothes never go to waste, Mason said.
lines.zh: 珍·梅森是大西洋沿岸小镇特拉华州刘易斯的“地下古着店”的老板。她说，店里卖不掉的衣服会送给当地人，他们把布料用于各种用途，比如做毯子。梅森说，卖不掉的衣服从不浪费。

lines.en: "We're a coastal community. So we're always thinking about how to be sustainable. And we also live on a peninsula, so, you know, it takes a lot (of) resources to get stuff out and back to here. So we're very much thinking about how to give something a new life."
lines.zh: “我们是个海滨社区，所以总是在想怎样才能可持续。我们还住在一个半岛上，你知道，把东西运出去再运回来要花很多资源。所以我们非常注重怎样让一样东西获得新生。”

lines.en: Large fashion companies are beginning to join the used clothing movement. Levis Secondhand is a new program from Levi Strauss & Co., the blue jeans manufacturer. The program buys back worn jeans to repurpose and resell them.
lines.zh: 大型时尚公司也开始加入旧衣运动。“李维斯二手”是牛仔裤制造商李维·斯特劳斯公司的一个新项目，回购穿过的牛仔裤，改造后再出售。

lines.en: The Fashion Industry Charter for Climate Action is an agreement under the U.N. to reduce greenhouse gasses. Organizations that sign the agreement promise to create fewer gasses linked to climate change. But many people buying clothing are hoping to help the environment by looking to the past.
lines.zh: 《时尚业气候行动宪章》是联合国框架下一项减少温室气体的协议。签署的机构承诺减少与气候变化有关的气体排放。但很多买衣服的人希望通过“回望过去”来帮助环境。

lines.en: A recent report in Utah's Deseret News notes that 20th century fashion is currently the most popular in Utah's used-clothing market.
lines.zh: 犹他州《德塞雷特新闻》最近的一篇报道指出，20 世纪的时装目前在犹他州的二手服装市场上最受欢迎。

lines.en: Delorean 88 is a vintage store in Washington, DC. Much of the store's clothing comes from the 1990s and early 2000s. The store carries mostly t-shirts, many with band logos and sports teams. One t-shirt features the faces of all the members of the 1996 Chicago Bulls, including Michael Jordan and Scottie Pippen, the team's stars. Another shirt is from the rap music performer Eminem after his first album released in 1999.
lines.zh: Delorean 88 是华盛顿的一家古着店。店里的衣服大多来自 20 世纪 90 年代和 21 世纪初，主要是 T 恤，很多印着乐队和运动队的标志。有一件 T 恤印着 1996 年芝加哥公牛队全体队员的头像，包括球队明星迈克尔·乔丹和斯科蒂·皮蓬。还有一件来自说唱歌手埃米纳姆 1999 年发行首张专辑之后。

lines.en: Michael Diaz works at the shop. He said customers have come in and noticed shirts their parents might have had.
lines.zh: 迈克尔·迪亚斯在这家店工作。他说，有顾客进店后认出了他们父母可能有过的 T 恤。

lines.en: "A store like this is just— it's nostalgia for a lot of people…They'd rather have this, like a shirt…that has, like 10 years of history, 20 years of history—rather wear that over a new shirt."
lines.zh: “像这样的店就是——对很多人来说是一种怀旧……他们宁愿要这个，比如一件有 10 年、20 年历史的 T 恤，也不愿穿一件新的。”

lines.en: Mason from Underground Vintage thinks part of the popularity in vintage shopping for younger people has to do with the time before the wide use of computers. Young people can disconnect from the internet and visit a physical store to try on clothes from a different time period. And the shop does not separate clothes for men and women.
lines.zh: “地下古着店”的梅森认为，古着在年轻人中流行，部分原因和电脑普及之前的那个时代有关。年轻人可以离开网络，去实体店试穿不同年代的衣服。而且店里不分男装女装。

lines.en: "So that's...another way that I think that vintage shopping really fits well with that generation—it's sustainable, it fits the goals of obviously having a planet to live on, but also having some pieces that mean something… You know, like we say on the sign ...wear what you like."
lines.zh: “所以这是……我认为古着购物非常适合那一代人的另一个原因——它是可持续的，显然符合拥有一个可以生存的星球的目标，同时也让人拥有一些有意义的衣服……就像我们招牌上写的……喜欢什么就穿什么。”

lines.en: I'm Dan Novak.
lines.zh: 我是丹·诺瓦克。

qs.q: Why do people buy vintage clothing?
opts: to save money and help the environment
because new clothes are not sold
because the government asks them to
qs.a: to save money and help the environment
qs.why: "buying old, used clothes can save money... good for the environment."

qs.q: What does Levi's Secondhand do?
opts: buys back worn jeans and resells them
qs.a: buys back worn jeans and resells them
qs.why: "The program buys back worn jeans to repurpose and resell them."

qs.q: What happens to unsold clothes at Underground Vintage?
opts: They are given to local people.
qs.a: They are given to local people.
qs.why: "clothes in the store that do not get sold are provided to local people."

lessons.title: Are America's Communities Disappearing?
lessons.zh: 美国的社区在消失吗？
lessons.sum: 《罗杰斯先生的邻居》教美国孩子善待邻里，可如今越来越少的美国人认识自己的邻居。作者邓克尔曼把人际关系分成内、中、外三圈，认为“中间圈”——邻居和社区——的减弱，正在削弱地方社区。

lines.en: "Won't you be my neighbor?" is a famous song from Mister Rogers' Neighborhood, a popular children's television show.
lines.zh: “你愿意做我的邻居吗？”是热门儿童电视节目《罗杰斯先生的邻居》里一首有名的歌。

lines.en: The show, broadcast for 31 years ending in 2001, sought to teach American children the importance of kindness and understanding towards others. The idea was that strong communities need strong relationships between the people in them.
lines.zh: 这个节目播了 31 年，2001 年结束，它想教美国孩子善良、理解他人的重要性。它的理念是：强大的社区需要社区里的人之间有牢固的关系。

lines.en: But fewer and fewer Americans seem to know their neighbors and that may be eroding America's communities.
lines.zh: 可是认识邻居的美国人似乎越来越少，这可能正在削弱美国的社区。

lines.en: Marc Dunkelman wrote a book called "The Vanishing Neighbor." In it, he examined how American communities have changed over time.
lines.zh: 马克·邓克尔曼写了一本书叫《消失的邻居》，探讨了美国社区如何随着时间变化。

lines.en: Dunkelman said most Americans have three levels of relationships: The inner circle includes family and close friends. The middle circle is more casual relationships. People in this circle include neighbors and people in community groups. The outer circle includes people who live far away but share a common interest. Today, people in outer circles are easily found through social media and other forms of technology.
lines.zh: 邓克尔曼说，大多数美国人有三层关系：内圈包括家人和亲密的朋友；中间圈是比较随意的关系，包括邻居和社区团体里的人；外圈包括住得很远但有共同兴趣的人。如今，通过社交媒体和其他技术很容易找到外圈的人。

lines.en: In his book, Dunkelman argued that people spend most of their time and attention on the inner and outer circles. But, he said the middle-circle is necessary to strengthening local communities. Relationships with neighbors are important for debate, hearing different ideas and finding compromise.
lines.zh: 邓克尔曼在书中提出，人们把大部分时间和精力都花在了内圈和外圈上。但他说，中间圈对加强地方社区是必不可少的。与邻居的关系对辩论、听取不同意见和找到妥协都很重要。

lines.en: Brad Birzer is a professor of history at Hillsdale College in Michigan. He said Americans are now more connected with national communities than with local communities.
lines.zh: 布拉德·比尔泽是密歇根州希尔斯代尔学院的历史学教授。他说，美国人现在和全国性群体的联系比和地方社区的联系更紧密。

lines.en: "We used to think of the community good as a local thing, and now we tend to think of it as the whole country," he said.
lines.zh: “我们过去认为公共利益是地方上的事，现在我们往往认为它是整个国家的事。”他说。

lines.en: Americans used to have more middle-circle relationships. Face-to-face interaction was unavoidable without cell phones or the internet. People also felt more of an obligation to join community organizations.
lines.zh: 美国人过去有更多中间圈的关系。没有手机和网络，面对面的交往是免不了的。人们也觉得自己更有义务加入社区组织。

lines.en: Dunkelman argues that modern life has made middle-circle relationships less important. He said globalization, education and more women in the workforce have resulted in fewer middle-circle interactions. He said the weakening of communities has led to political divisions in America.
lines.zh: 邓克尔曼认为，现代生活让中间圈的关系变得不那么重要了。他说，全球化、教育以及更多女性参加工作，导致中间圈的交往减少。他说，社区的削弱导致了美国的政治分裂。

lines.en: Americans now have less interaction with others who hold different political opinions. Less interaction with people who voted for the opposite party means "you begin to really be alienated from people who voted for the other side," Dunkelman said.
lines.zh: 如今，美国人与持不同政治观点的人交往少了。邓克尔曼说，和投票给对立党派的人交往少了，意味着“你开始真正疏远投票给另一方的人”。

lines.en: There are some good results from this change in personal interaction, however. It has become harder for hate groups like the Ku Klux Klan to organize at the local level. Doctors and health experts all over the world have been able to collaborate to deal with the coronavirus health crisis.
lines.zh: 不过，人际交往的这种变化也带来了一些好结果。像三K党这样的仇恨团体更难在地方上组织起来了。全世界的医生和卫生专家也能够合作应对新冠疫情这样的健康危机。

lines.en: However, Americans may be losing what it means to be a good neighbor, as Fred Rogers of "Mister Rogers' Neighborhood" taught.
lines.zh: 然而，美国人可能正在失去《罗杰斯先生的邻居》里弗雷德·罗杰斯所教的“做个好邻居”的意义。

lines.en: Today, society's problems like homelessness or poverty are not seen as local problems to solve, but national problems.
lines.zh: 如今，无家可归和贫困这样的社会问题不再被看作需要地方解决的问题，而是全国性的问题。

lines.en: Doing good for a neighbor is healthy "not just for our neighbor, but for ourselves as well," Dunkelman said. Learning how to be a good citizen can be lost, he said, "when we defer the problem to somebody else."
lines.zh: 邓克尔曼说，为邻居做好事是健康的，“不仅对我们的邻居，对我们自己也是”。他说，“当我们把问题推给别人时”，学习如何做一个好公民的机会就可能失去。

lines.en: I'm Caty Weaver.
lines.zh: 我是凯蒂·韦弗。

qs.q: Who is in the "middle circle"?
opts: neighbors and people in community groups
qs.a: neighbors and people in community groups
qs.why: "People in this circle include neighbors and people in community groups."

qs.q: Why did people have more middle-circle relationships before?
opts: There were no cell phones or internet.
qs.a: There were no cell phones or internet.
qs.why: "Face-to-face interaction was unavoidable without cell phones or the internet."

qs.q: What TV show taught children to be good neighbors?
qs.why: "a famous song from Mister Rogers' Neighborhood"

lessons.title: Baseball Fans Excited, Worried About Opening Day
lessons.zh: 棒球开幕日：球迷又兴奋又担心
lessons.sum: 2021 年美国职业棒球大联盟赛季 4 月 1 日开幕。这是新冠疫情后球迷第一次能回到球场，但各城市限制了观众人数，球迷们既兴奋又担心。对很多人来说，棒球赛季意味着春天和正常生活的回归。

lines.en: The Major League Baseball season in the U.S. begins on April 1. The first day of games is known as Opening Day.
lines.zh: 美国职业棒球大联盟赛季于 4 月 1 日开始。比赛的第一天叫“开幕日”。

lines.en: For most baseball fans, it is the first time they have been able to see their favorite teams and players since the end of the 2019 season.
lines.zh: 对大多数棒球迷来说，这是他们自 2019 赛季结束以来第一次能现场看到自己喜欢的球队和球员。

lines.en: In 2020, the season started late, and fans were not permitted to come to games during the COVID-19 pandemic.
lines.zh: 2020 年，赛季开始得晚，而且在新冠疫情期间球迷不准进场看比赛。

lines.en: By October, some fans could go to games in controlled environments called bubbles. The Los Angeles Dodgers won the season's final game and became champions.
lines.zh: 到 10 月，一些球迷可以在叫作“泡泡”的受控环境中看比赛。洛杉矶道奇队赢得了赛季最后一场比赛，成为冠军。

lines.en: Historically, Opening Day signals the arrival of spring after a long winter. And baseball fans are filled with excitement and optimism.
lines.zh: 历史上，开幕日标志着漫长冬天后春天的到来，棒球迷们充满兴奋和乐观。

lines.en: But this year will be different. Fans are still excited and optimistic, but they are also worried about returning to group events.
lines.zh: 可今年会不一样。球迷们仍然兴奋、乐观，但他们也担心回到人群聚集的活动中。

lines.en: The Washington Post conducted a poll of sports fans with the help of the University of Maryland. It found that less than half of Americans would feel comfortable attending a sporting event.
lines.zh: 《华盛顿邮报》在马里兰大学的帮助下对体育迷做了一项民意调查，发现不到一半的美国人会安心地去看体育比赛。

lines.en: More fans said they would feel better about attending an outdoor game like baseball compared to an indoor game such as basketball. Also, they would feel better about going to a game if fans were required to wear face coverings, tested for the virus or received a vaccine.
lines.zh: 更多球迷说，比起篮球这样的室内比赛，他们去看棒球这样的户外比赛会更放心。另外，如果要求观众戴口罩、做病毒检测或接种疫苗，他们去看比赛也会更放心。

lines.en: Cities around the U.S. with baseball teams are cutting back the number of fans who can attend. The famous New York Yankees baseball team will let about 10,000 fans attend the games. The fans will need to be vaccinated or tested for the virus.
lines.zh: 美国有棒球队的城市都在削减能进场的球迷人数。著名的纽约扬基队将允许约一万名球迷观看比赛，球迷需要接种疫苗或做病毒检测。

lines.en: In Washington, D.C., about 5,000 people will be able to go to games in the first part of the season. They will be required to sit apart from each other and keep their faces covered most of the time.
lines.zh: 在华盛顿，赛季前期约有 5000 人可以去看比赛。他们必须分开坐，大部分时间都要戴着口罩。

lines.en: "I hope that those 5,000, at least at the start who are allowed in, kind of realize how lucky they are just to be there. You know, 35,000 every night at least who would happily trade places with them and deal with the protocols in place."
lines.zh: “我希望至少在开始阶段获准入场的那 5000 人，能意识到自己能到场有多幸运。你知道，每晚至少有 35000 人乐意和他们换位置，也愿意遵守那些规定。”

lines.en: That is Scott Allen. He is a sports writer for the Washington Post.
lines.zh: 这是斯科特·艾伦，《华盛顿邮报》的体育记者。

lines.en: The poll from the Washington Post does note, however, that sports fans are more at ease with the idea of attending games today than they were at this time last year. About 65 percent said going to a game in May 2020 was "a large risk." Now that number is down to 26 percent.
lines.zh: 不过《华盛顿邮报》的调查也指出，与去年这个时候相比，体育迷现在对去看比赛的想法安心多了。大约 65% 的人说 2020 年 5 月去看比赛“风险很大”，现在这个数字降到了 26%。

lines.en: One person who is willing to take the risk is a baseball fan named Greg. He was walking with his family outside the Washington Nationals ballpark on Tuesday.
lines.zh: 一个愿意冒这个险的人是名叫格雷格的棒球迷。星期二，他和家人在华盛顿国民队的球场外散步。

lines.en: "I'm excited," he said. "I'm taking my dad. I missed sitting in the seats, watching the game and drinking a beer. Just the whole ballpark atmosphere."
lines.zh: “我很兴奋，”他说，“我要带我爸爸去。我想念坐在座位上看比赛、喝啤酒的感觉。就是整个球场的氛围。”

lines.en: There were others, however, who wanted to wait and see how the first part of the season went before going back to the games.
lines.zh: 不过也有人想先看看赛季前期的情况，再回球场看比赛。

lines.en: Dan Sullivan was with a friend at a coffee shop near the Washington Nationals home. He said he will wait to be vaccinated before going to a game. He does not mind missing Opening Day.
lines.zh: 丹·沙利文和一个朋友在华盛顿国民队主场附近的一家咖啡店里。他说他会等打完疫苗再去看比赛，错过开幕日也无所谓。

lines.en: "I hope the people who are there are going to enjoy it, but most people are not there," he said. Since so few fans are allowed, he does not feel as if he is missing out.
lines.zh: “我希望到场的人能玩得开心，但大多数人都不在场。”他说。因为允许入场的球迷太少，他并不觉得自己错过了什么。

lines.en: Allen, the Washington Post writer, said even with Opening Day being so different, he thinks fans will see it as a return to normalcy.
lines.zh: 《华盛顿邮报》记者艾伦说，尽管今年的开幕日如此不同，他认为球迷们会把它看作回归正常的标志。

lines.en: "[The baseball season] is way to mark time and important moments in your life. People couldn't do that last year, and I think it hurt them. It feels more like the start of spring and what should be an enjoyable summer when you know that almost every day you're going to be able to turn on the baseball game, or go to see your favorite team."
lines.zh: “（棒球赛季）是记录时间和人生重要时刻的一种方式。去年人们做不到，我想这伤害了他们。当你知道几乎每天都能打开电视看棒球、或者去看你喜欢的球队时，这更像是春天的开始，也预示着一个本该愉快的夏天。”

lines.en: I'm Dan Friedell.
lines.zh: 我是丹·弗里德尔。

qs.q: What is "Opening Day"?
opts: the first day of the baseball season
qs.a: the first day of the baseball season
qs.why: "The first day of games is known as Opening Day."

qs.q: How many fans could go to games in Washington at first?
qs.why: "about 5,000 people will be able to go to games."

qs.q: What does Opening Day traditionally signal?
qs.why: "Opening Day signals the arrival of spring after a long winter."

lessons.title: Ten Restaurants that Changed How Americans Eat
lessons.zh: 改变美国人饮食的十家餐馆
lessons.sum: 耶鲁大学历史学家弗里德曼选出十家改变美国人饮食的餐馆：从 1830 年纽约的第一家餐馆德尔莫尼科，到公路连锁店霍华德·约翰逊、旧金山的高档中餐馆、哈莱姆的南方菜馆，再到倡导本地应季食材的伯克利 Chez Panisse。

lines.en: America's first restaurant was called Delmonico's. It started in 1830 in New York. And Yale University history professor Paul Freedman says it had a big effect on the food Americans eat.
lines.zh: 美国的第一家餐馆叫德尔莫尼科，1830 年在纽约开张。耶鲁大学历史学教授保罗·弗里德曼说，它对美国人的饮食有很大影响。

lines.en: "It defined what elegant food was in the 19th century United States, and that has influenced…the food that is eaten today," Freedman said.
lines.zh: “它定义了 19 世纪美国的高档食物是什么样，这影响了……今天人们吃的食物。”弗里德曼说。

lines.en: Delmonico's invented famous foods like lobster Newberg and baked Alaska. It continues to serve those and other favorites at its New York City location.
lines.zh: 德尔莫尼科发明了纽堡龙虾和火焰雪山（烤阿拉斯加）等名菜，至今仍在纽约店里供应这些和其他招牌菜。

lines.en: "It's created in the 1830s, but in 1890, it's still considered the best restaurant in the U.S.," Freedman said. A lot of restaurants elsewhere called themselves "the Delmonico's of" whatever city they were in, he added.
lines.zh: “它是 19 世纪 30 年代创办的，但到了 1890 年，它仍被认为是美国最好的餐馆。”弗里德曼说。他还说，其他地方的很多餐馆都自称是所在城市的“德尔莫尼科”。

lines.en: In his book, "Ten Restaurants That Changed America," Freedman names nine other restaurants that greatly influenced what Americans eat.
lines.zh: 弗里德曼在他的书《改变美国的十家餐馆》中，列出了另外九家对美国人饮食影响很大的餐馆。

lines.en: "I chose them both for just the delight of restaurants as places, but also as a way of talking about American history," he says. "Because you can't talk about restaurants without talking about ethnicity, immigration…and different social settings. So, this was intended… as a history of American society seen through its restaurants."
lines.zh: “我选它们，一方面是因为餐馆作为场所本身的乐趣，另一方面也是借此讲美国的历史，”他说，“因为谈餐馆，就不能不谈族裔、移民……和不同的社会环境。所以这本书本来就是……一部透过餐馆看美国社会的历史。”

lines.en: Howard Johnson's is on the list. It was one of America's first chain restaurants. A chain restaurant provides exactly the same food selections no matter which restaurant a person visits.
lines.zh: 霍华德·约翰逊餐厅在名单上。它是美国最早的连锁餐厅之一。连锁餐厅就是不管去哪一家，提供的菜品都完全一样。

lines.en: Howard Johnson's were built along highways. "It was roadside food. It was chain food. It pioneered the franchise as a way of expansion, Freedman said. The company's founder, Howard Deering Johnson, built his restaurants so that drivers could easily identify them, he added.
lines.zh: 霍华德·约翰逊餐厅建在公路沿线。“这是路边的食物，连锁的食物。它开创了以特许经营来扩张的方式。”弗里德曼说。他还说，公司创始人霍华德·迪林·约翰逊把餐厅建得让司机一眼就能认出来。

lines.en: Howard Johnson's did not survive the competition it helped create, like McDonald's and other fast-food restaurants.
lines.zh: 霍华德·约翰逊餐厅没能在它帮助开创的竞争中幸存下来，比如麦当劳和其他快餐店。

lines.en: Also on the list is the Mandarin, a Chinese restaurant opened in San Francisco in 1961 by Cecilia Chang. She remade Americans' idea of Chinese food, making it luxurious, Freedman said.
lines.zh: 名单上还有“福禄寿”（the Mandarin），这是江孙芸 1961 年在旧金山开的一家中餐馆。弗里德曼说，她重塑了美国人对中餐的看法，让它变得高档奢华。

lines.en: Other women-run restaurants Freedman writes about include Sylvia's in Harlem. Born in South Carolina, Sylvia Woods brought Southern cooking and the idea of a neighborhood restaurant as a community gathering place to New York.
lines.zh: 弗里德曼写到的其他由女性经营的餐馆还有哈莱姆的“西尔维娅”。西尔维娅·伍兹出生在南卡罗来纳州，她把南方菜，以及把街坊餐馆当作社区聚会场所的理念带到了纽约。

lines.en: It "is also an example of the story of African American migration from the South to the North," Freedman said.
lines.zh: 弗里德曼说，它“也是非裔美国人从南方迁往北方的故事的一个例子”。

lines.en: Mamma Leone's, also in New York, helped bring Italian food to the American people. Luisa Leone opened her eatery in 1906 and was able to expand beyond Italian American diners. She created a model for other immigrant business owners to follow.
lines.zh: 同样在纽约的“利昂妈妈”帮助把意大利菜带给了美国人。路易莎·利昂在 1906 年开了这家餐馆，顾客不只限于意大利裔美国人。她为其他移民店主树立了一个可以效仿的榜样。

lines.en: "Mamma Leone's served something like 3,000 people a day, many of them tourists, so a lot of people got their idea of what Italian food ought to be," Freedman said.
lines.zh: “利昂妈妈每天大约接待 3000 人，很多是游客，所以很多人就是从那里形成了意大利菜应该是什么样的印象。”弗里德曼说。

lines.en: Alice Waters opened Chez Panisse in Berkeley, California, in 1971. She changed American cooking by using only local and in-season foods - a tradition that continues today.
lines.zh: 艾丽斯·沃特斯 1971 年在加利福尼亚州伯克利开了 Chez Panisse 餐厅。她只用本地应季食材，改变了美国的烹饪——这个传统一直延续到今天。

lines.en: Although these female restaurateurs served widely different foods, they all created restaurants that valued quality food.
lines.zh: 虽然这几位女餐馆老板做的菜差别很大，但她们开的餐馆都重视食物的质量。

lines.en: It "was familiar but better," Freedman said. "Better than the competition."
lines.zh: 弗里德曼说，那是“熟悉的，但更好。比竞争对手更好”。

lines.en: The other restaurants on Freedman's list include The Four Seasons in New York. It opened in 1959 and offered American food at a time when French food was popular.
lines.zh: 弗里德曼名单上的其他餐馆包括纽约的“四季”。它 1959 年开张，在法国菜流行的时候供应美国菜。

lines.en: He includes Le Pavillon in New York, Antoine's in New Orleans and Schrafft's in Boston.
lines.zh: 他还列入了纽约的 Le Pavillon、新奥尔良的 Antoine's 和波士顿的 Schrafft's。

lines.en: Most of Freedman's picks are on the East or West Coast.
lines.zh: 弗里德曼选的餐馆大多在东海岸或西海岸。

lines.en: "I think it has to do with New York and San Francisco being ports, and so, the first place where immigrants opened up restaurants," he said.
lines.zh: “我想这和纽约、旧金山是港口有关，所以那里是移民最先开餐馆的地方。”他说。

lines.en: I'm Jill Robbins.
lines.zh: 我是吉尔·罗宾斯。

qs.q: What was America's first restaurant?
qs.why: "America's first restaurant was called Delmonico's."

qs.q: What is a chain restaurant?
opts: one that serves the same food at every location
qs.a: one that serves the same food at every location
qs.why: "provides exactly the same food selections no matter which restaurant a person visits."

qs.q: What did Alice Waters change?
opts: She used only local and in-season foods.
She brought Chinese food to San Francisco.
qs.a: She used only local and in-season foods.
qs.why: "by using only local and in-season foods."

lessons.title: What Is the Most Popular Ethnic Food in the US?
lessons.zh: 美国最受欢迎的异国美食是什么？
lessons.sum: 根据谷歌搜索数据，墨西哥菜是最多州最受欢迎的异国美食，尤其在西海岸；但在全国范围内中餐排第一。泰国、韩国、越南、日本餐馆也越来越受欢迎，千禧一代是推动饮食多样化的主力。

lines.en: For years, the United States has been called a melting pot – a place where different individuals or groups of people are mixed together. And the country's food preferences show that.
lines.zh: 多年来，美国一直被称为“熔炉”——一个不同个人和群体融合在一起的地方。这个国家的饮食偏好也体现了这一点。

lines.en: Many Americans learn about and enjoy different cultures through food. One study shows that Mexican food is the most popular ethnic food in the largest number of states. It is especially popular on the U.S. West Coast. But Chinese food is the top ethnic food nationwide.
lines.zh: 许多美国人通过食物了解和享受不同的文化。一项研究显示，在最多的州里，墨西哥菜是最受欢迎的异国美食，在美国西海岸尤其受欢迎。但在全国范围内，中餐是排名第一的异国美食。

lines.en: "Both cuisines have a rich history connected to the large immigrant Chinese and Mexican populations in the U.S." notes Georgie Mihaila. She is with a food-based blog called Chef's Pencil.
lines.zh: “这两种菜系都有丰富的历史，与美国大量的中国和墨西哥移民人口有关。”乔治·米哈伊拉指出。她在一个叫“厨师的铅笔”的美食博客工作。

lines.en: The website was the idea of professional chefs, the men and women who prepare meals for top restaurants. It used information from Google's search engine to identify the most popular ethnic food in the country.
lines.zh: 这个网站是一些专业厨师——为顶级餐馆做菜的男女厨师——的主意。它利用谷歌搜索引擎的信息，找出全国最受欢迎的异国美食。

lines.en: Mihaila said that as generations of immigrants settled in the U.S., they made their food more readily available -- and less costly.
lines.zh: 米哈伊拉说，随着一代代移民在美国定居，他们让自己的食物更容易买到，也更便宜。

lines.en: Thai, Korean, Vietnamese and Japanese restaurants are also gaining fans across the country. Their popularity is no accident, either.
lines.zh: 泰国、韩国、越南和日本餐馆在全国也越来越受欢迎。它们的流行也不是偶然的。

lines.en: In 2002, for example, Thailand's government started training chefs and sending them out to share their cuisine with the world. The aim of the "Global Thai" culinary diplomacy program was to increase the number of Thai restaurants worldwide.
lines.zh: 比如在 2002 年，泰国政府开始培训厨师，把他们派到世界各地分享泰国菜。这个“全球泰国”美食外交项目的目的，是增加全世界泰国餐馆的数量。

lines.en: Millennials are leading the push for more diverse food experiences. Millennials are now the nation's largest age group. They are generally between the ages of 26 and 40. And they are likely to share their eating experiences on social media.
lines.zh: 千禧一代正在推动更多样的饮食体验。千禧一代如今是美国人数最多的年龄群体，年龄大致在 26 到 40 岁之间。他们很可能在社交媒体上分享自己的用餐体验。

lines.en: "It's not just about the food, but also the atmosphere, the culture, about ...experiencing something fun and memorable," Mihaila said.
lines.zh: “这不只是关于食物，还关于氛围、文化，关于……体验一些有趣又难忘的东西。”米哈伊拉说。

lines.en: In general, she added, Americans are making more adventurous food choices.
lines.zh: 她补充说，总的来说，美国人在饮食上越来越敢于尝试。

lines.en: "Many of them are seeking new experiences, both when dining out and when cooking for themselves," she said. "I think the pandemic was a great example of that with people trying out more foods that they would cook at home."
lines.zh: “他们很多人在寻找新的体验，不管是出去吃饭还是自己做饭，”她说，“我觉得疫情就是一个很好的例子，人们在家尝试做更多不同的食物。”

lines.en: Often, Chinese, Mexican and other ethnic food restaurants are less pricey than other eateries.
lines.zh: 通常，中餐、墨西哥菜和其他异国美食餐馆比其他餐馆便宜。

lines.en: But that is also changing.
lines.zh: 不过这一点也在改变。

lines.en: Mihaila said, "You have restaurants opening up across the country that are serving ethnic foods like Mexican, Thai or Indian, that are positioned to serve the upper end of the market."
lines.zh: 米哈伊拉说：“全国各地都有餐馆开张，供应墨西哥、泰国或印度菜等异国美食，而且定位在高端市场。”

lines.en: Such businesses, she added, have seen great success.
lines.zh: 她补充说，这样的餐馆非常成功。

lines.en: I'm Ashley Thompson.
lines.zh: 我是阿什莉·汤普森。

qs.q: Which is the top ethnic food nationwide?
qs.why: "Chinese food is the top ethnic food nationwide."

qs.q: Which group is leading the push for diverse food?
qs.why: "Millennials are leading the push for more diverse food experiences."

qs.q: What did Thailand's government do in 2002?
opts: trained chefs and sent them abroad
qs.a: trained chefs and sent them abroad
qs.why: "Thailand's government started training chefs and sending them out."

lessons.title: Things You (Probably) Don't Know About the 4th of July
lessons.zh: 关于 7 月 4 日你（可能）不知道的事
lessons.sum: 独立日的冷知识：约翰·亚当斯原以为人们会庆祝 7 月 2 日；亚当斯、杰斐逊和门罗三位总统都在 7 月 4 日去世，柯立芝总统在这天出生；纽约康尼岛每年举行吃热狗大赛；美国人很爱烟花，但烟花和国旗大多是进口的。

lines.en: The United States observes its Independence Day on July 4th.
lines.zh: 美国在 7 月 4 日庆祝独立日。

lines.en: It normally includes massive public celebrations of music, fireworks and food in cities and towns across the country. This year, however, much of the country is avoiding large gatherings, or barring them.
lines.zh: 平常，这一天全国各地的城镇都会举办盛大的公共庆祝活动，有音乐、烟花和美食。不过今年，全国许多地方都在避免甚至禁止大型聚会。

lines.en: So, we are turning to the ghost of Independence Day past to note some lesser-known history of the holiday.
lines.zh: 所以，我们请出“往昔独立日的幽灵”，来讲讲这个节日一些鲜为人知的历史。

lines.en: This day will be remembered in American history, wrote John Adams in 1776. People will honor it with fireworks and celebrations.
lines.zh: 约翰·亚当斯在 1776 年写道，这一天将载入美国史册，人们会用烟花和庆祝活动来纪念它。

lines.en: He was talking about the second of July.
lines.zh: 他说的是 7 月 2 日。

lines.en: That is the day the Continental Congress voted in favor of independence from the British. The colonies officially became self-ruling states.
lines.zh: 那天大陆会议投票赞成脱离英国独立，各殖民地正式成为自治的州。

lines.en: But the date written on the Declaration of Independence is July 4. So, since 1776, Americans have honored July 4 as the country's Independence Day.
lines.zh: 可《独立宣言》上写的日期是 7 月 4 日。所以自 1776 年以来，美国人一直把 7 月 4 日当作国家的独立日。

lines.en: And July 2? Not so much.
lines.zh: 那 7 月 2 日呢？就没那么受重视了。

lines.en: Adams went on to become the first vice-president of the United States of America and its second president. He observed many July 4th Independence Days right up until he died --- on July 4th, 1826. That same day, a few hours earlier, Adams' lifelong friend, opponent, former vice president, and third president, Thomas Jefferson, also died.
lines.zh: 亚当斯后来成为美国第一任副总统和第二任总统。他过了许多个 7 月 4 日独立日，直到去世——1826 年 7 月 4 日。同一天，几个小时前，亚当斯一生的朋友、对手、前副总统和第三任总统托马斯·杰斐逊也去世了。

lines.en: It was the 50th anniversary of Independence Day.
lines.zh: 那天正是独立日 50 周年。

lines.en: Five years later, James Monroe, the country's fifth president, also died on July 4.
lines.zh: 五年后，美国第五任总统詹姆斯·门罗也在 7 月 4 日去世。

lines.en: And one president, Calvin Coolidge, was born on July 4, in 1872.
lines.zh: 还有一位总统卡尔文·柯立芝，于 1872 年 7 月 4 日出生。

lines.en: Most Americans celebrate Independence Day with barbecues, parades and, yes, fireworks. But a few celebrate by eating all the hot dogs they can.
lines.zh: 大多数美国人用烧烤、游行，当然还有烟花来庆祝独立日。不过也有少数人用尽情吃热狗来庆祝。

lines.en: Every July 4th since the early 1970s, a restaurant called Nathan's Famous has held a competition to see who can eat the most hot dogs in ten minutes. The event involves 30 to 40 competitors divided by sex. Women face women. Men face men.
lines.zh: 自 20 世纪 70 年代初以来，每年 7 月 4 日，一家叫 Nathan's Famous 的餐馆都会举办比赛，看谁能在十分钟内吃最多的热狗。比赛有 30 到 40 名选手，按性别分组：女子对女子，男子对男子。

lines.en: The competition is held at Nathan's Famous in the Coney Island area of New York City. The 1916 restaurant grew over the years into a large food business, with many stores.
lines.zh: 比赛在纽约市康尼岛地区的 Nathan's Famous 举行。这家 1916 年开张的餐馆多年来发展成一家有许多门店的大型食品企业。

lines.en: The undeniable star eater at Nathan's is Joey Chestnut of California. The 36-year-old has won the men's championship 12 times, including last year. He also holds the Nathan's record for most hot dogs eaten in competition --- 74.
lines.zh: Nathan's 无可争议的吃货明星是加利福尼亚的乔伊·切斯特纳特。这位 36 岁的选手已经 12 次获得男子冠军，包括去年。他还保持着 Nathan's 比赛中吃热狗最多的纪录——74 个。

lines.en: New York native Miki Sudo is Nathan's Famous current women's champion. She has won the event six times, more than any other woman.
lines.zh: 纽约人苏多美纪是 Nathan's Famous 目前的女子冠军。她已经六次夺冠，比其他任何女选手都多。

lines.en: But her opponent, South Korean-born Sonya Thomas has eaten more hot dogs at the event. Thomas set the record in 2011 downing 40 hot dogs in ten minutes. But, that record did not last long. Thomas returned to Nathan's the following year and ate 45.
lines.zh: 不过她的对手、出生于韩国的索尼娅·托马斯在比赛中吃过更多热狗。托马斯在 2011 年创下纪录，十分钟吃下 40 个热狗。但这个纪录没保持多久，托马斯第二年又来参赛，吃了 45 个。

lines.en: Nathan's is holding the hot dog eating competition again this Independence Day. The event is not open to the public because of COVID-19. But, it will be covered live on television and the web.
lines.zh: 今年独立日，Nathan's 再次举办吃热狗比赛。由于新冠疫情，比赛不对公众开放，但会在电视和网上直播。

lines.en: So, let's go back to those fireworks, probably the most common image linked to Independence Day. Americans really, really love fireworks. The American Pyrotechnic Association – "pyrotechnic" is another word for "fireworks" – reported that Americans spent $1 billion on ordinary fireworks last year. And, the industry group said it also earned $375 million from sales of professional fireworks.
lines.zh: 好了，回到烟花吧，这可能是与独立日联系最紧密的形象了。美国人真的非常非常爱烟花。美国烟火协会——pyrotechnic 是“烟花”的另一个说法——报告说，去年美国人在普通烟花上花了 10 亿美元。这个行业组织还说，专业烟花的销售额达到 3.75 亿美元。

lines.en: But although fireworks are in popular use in America, they are rarely made in America. The huge majority is imported from China.
lines.zh: 不过，虽然烟花在美国很流行，却很少是美国制造的，绝大多数从中国进口。

lines.en: And, most American flags are made there too!
lines.zh: 而且大多数美国国旗也是在那里做的！

lines.en: Happy Independence Day!
lines.zh: 独立日快乐！

lines.en: I'm Caty Weaver.
lines.zh: 我是凯蒂·韦弗。

qs.q: Which date did John Adams think people would celebrate?
qs.why: "He was talking about the second of July."

qs.q: Which president was born on July 4?
qs.why: "Calvin Coolidge, was born on July 4, in 1872."

qs.q: What is the Nathan's Famous contest?
opts: eating the most hot dogs in ten minutes
qs.a: eating the most hot dogs in ten minutes
qs.why: "to see who can eat the most hot dogs in ten minutes."

lessons.title: US Botanic Garden Celebrates 200 Years
lessons.zh: 美国植物园 200 岁了
lessons.sum: 位于华盛顿国家广场、紧邻国会大厦的美国植物园成立于 1820 年，有 6.5 万株植物，其中有些已超过 165 岁。这里有热带和沙漠温室、4000 株兰花、圣诞小火车展，还有罕见的、开花时奇臭无比的“尸花”。

lines.en: Visitors come to the United States Botanic Garden in Washington, D.C. to enjoy many different plants, and the peace of nature.
lines.zh: 游客来到华盛顿的美国植物园，欣赏各种各样的植物，享受大自然的宁静。

lines.en: Anna Pavlova works nearby. She likes to come on short breaks during her workday, to find some peace.
lines.zh: 安娜·帕夫洛娃在附近工作。她喜欢在工作间隙来这里歇一会儿，找一份宁静。

lines.en: "It feels like a forest in a city so I can be thinking about something else besides work for even five minutes which is sometimes very nice."
lines.zh: “这里感觉就像城市里的一片森林，哪怕只有五分钟，我也能想想工作以外的事，有时候真的很好。”

lines.en: This year, the U.S. Botanic Garden celebrates its 200th anniversary. It was founded by two U.S. Presidents; George Washington and Thomas Jefferson. Established in 1820, the Garden collects and grows plants. Its mission is to demonstrate the aesthetic, cultural, economic, therapeutic and ecological importance of plants to the well-being of humankind.
lines.zh: 今年，美国植物园庆祝成立 200 周年。它由两位美国总统——乔治·华盛顿和托马斯·杰斐逊——创立，1820 年建成，收集和种植植物。它的使命是展示植物在美学、文化、经济、身心健康和生态方面对人类福祉的重要性。

lines.en: The Garden on the National Mall is just down a hill from the U.S. Capitol building. The garden is made up of 65,000 indoor and outdoor plants. Some are more than 165 years old. Workers document and care for the plants. They are shared with the public for study purposes as well as pleasure.
lines.zh: 植物园位于国家广场，就在美国国会大厦所在的山坡下。园内有 6.5 万株室内和户外植物，有些已有 165 年以上的历史。工作人员记录并照料这些植物，供公众研究和观赏。

lines.en: The Garden's conservatory, or greenhouse is a beautiful glass and steel building. Sunlight floods in, helping the plants grow. Rooms inside are home to plants that do well in different environments. For example, there is the warm and damp tropical room as well as the one that has desert conditions.
lines.zh: 植物园的温室是一座漂亮的玻璃和钢结构建筑。阳光洒进来，帮助植物生长。里面的各个房间适合在不同环境中生长的植物，比如有温暖潮湿的热带馆，也有模拟沙漠环境的展馆。

lines.en: Saharah Moon Chapotin is Executive Director of the U.S. Botanic Garden.
lines.zh: 萨哈拉·穆恩·查波廷是美国植物园的执行主任。

lines.en: She told VOA that "we still have a very important role to play in educating people about the importance of plants." She said this is especially true for people who live in cities, and may not have a connection to a farm, or clearly understand where food comes from.
lines.zh: 她对 VOA 说：“在教育人们认识植物的重要性方面，我们仍然扮演着非常重要的角色。”她说，对住在城市里的人来说尤其如此，他们可能和农场没什么联系，也不太清楚食物从哪里来。

lines.en: The newest exhibit, "Deeply Rooted, Branching Outward" covers the scientific exploration of plants. Chapotin hopes the garden will give visitors a "greater appreciation for plants," and how they help with every part of our daily lives.
lines.zh: 最新的展览“根深叶茂”介绍了对植物的科学探索。查波廷希望植物园能让游客“更加欣赏植物”，了解它们如何帮助我们日常生活的方方面面。

lines.en: Among the garden's most loved plants are the 4,000 orchid that come from around the world. During the spring orchid show each year, many flowers bloom, including some that are endangered.
lines.zh: 园里最受喜爱的植物之一，是来自世界各地的 4000 株兰花。每年春季兰花展期间，许多花都会开放，其中包括一些濒危品种。

lines.en: During the Christmas season, a very popular exhibit has toy trains on tracks, moving through plants and structures made from plant-based materials.
lines.zh: 圣诞季期间，一个很受欢迎的展览是玩具火车在轨道上穿行于植物和用植物材料制作的建筑之间。

lines.en: Another popular event at the Garden is the flowering of the rare, huge "corpse flower." It can go years in between blooms. The plant can grow to over 8 feet tall, and it known for its horrible smell—sometimes described as the smell of death.
lines.zh: 植物园另一个受欢迎的活动是罕见的巨型“尸花”开花。它可能好几年才开一次花。这种植物能长到 8 英尺以上，以气味难闻出名——有时被形容为死亡的气味。

lines.en: Something decidedly sweeter is the smell of roses when the weather turns warm in Washington, D.C. Many varieties and colors of these beautiful flowers, along with other outdoor plants, bloom at the Garden when warm weather and sunshine comes to town.
lines.zh: 天气转暖时，华盛顿的玫瑰花香可就甜美多了。温暖的天气和阳光来到城里时，植物园里许多品种、各种颜色的美丽玫瑰和其他户外植物都会开放。

lines.en: That is when you find visitors and workers taking a break, walking the outdoor paths, looking at the water structures, and maybe even stopping to smell the roses.
lines.zh: 那时你会看到游客和上班族在这里歇一歇，在户外小径上散步，看看水景，甚至停下来闻闻玫瑰花香。

lines.en: I'm Anne Ball.
lines.zh: 我是安妮·鲍尔。

qs.q: When was the US Botanic Garden established?
qs.why: "Established in 1820..."

qs.q: What is special about the "corpse flower"?
qs.why: "known for its horrible smell."

qs.q: Why does Anna Pavlova visit the garden?
opts: to find some peace during work breaks
qs.a: to find some peace during work breaks
qs.why: "She likes to come on short breaks during her workday, to find some peace."

lessons.title: Balloon Festivals Celebrate First Method of Human Flight
lessons.zh: 热气球节：庆祝人类最早的飞行方式
lessons.sum: 1783 年，两位法国人乘热气球飞过巴黎，比莱特兄弟早一百多年。如今世界各地都有热气球节：日本佐贺的夜间灯光、墨西哥莱昂的“飞屋”，以及全球最大的美国新墨西哥州阿尔伯克基热气球节。

lines.en: The path of human aviation is uneven and dangerous. But, from the ancient story of an English king killed in his attempt to fly with handmade wings to the launchings of rockets to the International Space Station, the desire for flight continues.
lines.zh: 人类的航空之路坎坷而危险。可是，从一位英国国王戴着手工翅膀试飞而丧生的古老故事，到向国际空间站发射火箭，人类对飞行的渴望从未停止。

lines.en: Some people think of the American brothers Wilbur and Orville Wright as the first pilots of the sky. In 1903, the two men made four brief flights in a powered plane in North Carolina.
lines.zh: 有些人认为美国的威尔伯·莱特和奥维尔·莱特兄弟是第一批飞上天空的人。1903 年，两人在北卡罗来纳州驾驶一架动力飞机进行了四次短暂飞行。

lines.en: But more than 100 years earlier, two Frenchmen were actually the first to float through the sky.
lines.zh: 但在那之前一百多年，两个法国人才是真正最早在天空中飘飞的人。

lines.en: On November 21, 1783, Jean François Pilâtre de Rozier and Marquis d'Arlandes got into a small open airboat. Above their heads, long ropes attached the craft to a huge hot air balloon. The balloon rose slowly, carrying its pilots over a public park in Paris.
lines.zh: 1783 年 11 月 21 日，让-弗朗索瓦·皮拉特尔·德罗齐耶和达朗德侯爵登上一只小小的敞篷吊篮。他们头顶上，长长的绳子把吊篮和一个巨大的热气球连在一起。气球缓缓升起，载着两位驾驶员飞过巴黎的一座公园。

lines.en: In 1785, two other pilots flew a similar airship across the English Channel.
lines.zh: 1785 年，另外两名驾驶员驾驶一艘类似的飞艇飞越了英吉利海峡。

lines.en: Although it never became a main form of transportation, balloon flight has stuck.
lines.zh: 虽然热气球从未成为主要的交通工具，但它一直流传了下来。

lines.en: Today, hot air balloon fans celebrate the aircraft in festivals around the world. Hundreds of thousands recently attended the largest such event, held in Albuquerque, New Mexico. The León International Balloon Festival just closed in Mexico. Similar celebrations take place in Canada, France and Japan, to name a few. Today, we explore a few of these events.
lines.zh: 如今，热气球爱好者在世界各地的节日上庆祝这种飞行器。几十万人最近参加了规模最大的热气球节——在新墨西哥州阿尔伯克基举行。墨西哥的莱昂国际热气球节也刚刚结束。加拿大、法国和日本等地也有类似的庆祝活动。今天我们就来看看其中几个。

lines.en: In Saga, Japan, more than 100 balloons from about 20 countries take part in a five-day competition and celebration. Competitors are tested on flight control and other skills.
lines.zh: 在日本佐贺，来自约 20 个国家的 100 多只热气球参加为期五天的比赛和庆祝活动。参赛者要接受飞行控制等技能的考验。

lines.en: Balloons rise into the air from along the Kase River each day. Others are launched elsewhere, and can be seen in the air over homes and other buildings.
lines.zh: 每天，气球从嘉濑川沿岸升空，还有一些从别处放飞，可以看到它们飘在房屋和其他建筑上空。

lines.en: However, one of the most beautiful sights at the Saga International Balloon Festival happens after dark, during La Montgolfier Nocturne. Known as the Night Mooring in English, the event involves balloons lining up on the riverside. The balloons all light up at once from the firing of their burners. The result is an extensive, extraordinary glow, which is reflected in the river.
lines.zh: 不过，佐贺国际热气球节最美的景象之一出现在天黑以后，那就是“夜间系留”活动。热气球沿河边排成一排，同时点燃燃烧器，一起亮起来，形成一大片非凡的光芒，倒映在河面上。

lines.en: The balloon fiesta in Saga takes place yearly in early November.
lines.zh: 佐贺热气球节每年 11 月初举行。

lines.en: Next we travel to the central Mexican city of León. The yearly balloon celebration there is known as FIG, for Festival Internacional del Globo. The 2019 event took place from November 15-18.
lines.zh: 接下来我们去墨西哥中部城市莱昂。那里一年一度的热气球节叫 FIG，即“国际热气球节”。2019 年的活动在 11 月 15 日到 18 日举行。

lines.en: The FIG is the biggest balloon festival in Latin America. About 200 hot air balloons and pilots from 15 different countries are involved. Hundreds of thousands of visitors attend.
lines.zh: FIG 是拉丁美洲最大的热气球节，有来自 15 个国家的约 200 只热气球和驾驶员参加，参观者达几十万人。

lines.en: The first FIG took place in 2002 with just 25 balloons. Its website says that year, the event "began the magic and the first experience of seeing this dream fly by painting the sky of León…"
lines.zh: 第一届 FIG 在 2002 年举行，只有 25 只气球。它的网站说，那一年，这个活动“开启了魔法，让人们第一次看到这个梦想飞过，描绘了莱昂的天空……”

lines.en: At the 2014 FIG, American aviator Jonathan Trappe made history and paid respects to the beloved American film Up. The pilot attached dozens of balloons to an airboat that looked much like the house in the 2009 film. Then, just like the character Carl in the movie, Trappe floated the house up into the air. He traveled over Mexico that way for several days.
lines.zh: 在 2014 年的 FIG 上，美国飞行员乔纳森·特拉普创造了历史，也向深受喜爱的美国电影《飞屋环游记》致敬。他把几十个气球绑在一个很像 2009 年那部电影里房子的吊舱上，然后像电影里的卡尔一样，让房子飘上了天空。他就这样在墨西哥上空飞了好几天。

lines.en: Like at other festivals, the balloons come in different colors and shapes. Visitors might look up and see the Disney character Mickey Mouse. Or they might see a yellow smiley face, a giant heart, a space creature or a clown and zebra flying side by side.
lines.zh: 和其他热气球节一样，这里的气球颜色各异、形状不同。游客抬头可能会看到迪士尼的米老鼠，也可能看到黄色笑脸、巨大的爱心、外星生物，或者小丑和斑马并肩飞翔。

lines.en: The biggest hot air balloon festival in the world takes place in the American city of Albuquerque, New Mexico. It is called the Albuquerque International Balloon Fiesta.
lines.zh: 世界上最大的热气球节在美国新墨西哥州阿尔伯克基市举行，叫作“阿尔伯克基国际热气球节”。

lines.en: Organizers of the event say more than 850,000 people attended the nine-day event this year. There were almost 600 balloons and 671 pilots from around the world.
lines.zh: 活动组织者说，今年为期九天的活动有 85 万多人参加，有来自世界各地的近 600 只气球和 671 名驾驶员。

lines.en: The fiesta also appeals to photographers, both professional and amateur. It has long included a competition for best pictures of the celebration. That contest is named in honor of Cindy Petrehn, the official photographer of the Albuquerque festival until her death in 2013. Petrehn was also a balloon pilot herself. She captured images from and of hot air balloons all over the world.
lines.zh: 这个节日也吸引了专业和业余摄影师。它一直设有一项最佳节日照片比赛。比赛以辛迪·佩特雷恩的名字命名，她是阿尔伯克基热气球节的官方摄影师，2013 年去世。佩特雷恩自己也是热气球驾驶员，她在世界各地拍摄热气球，也从热气球上拍摄。

lines.en: In this year's photography contest, Jeff Wamer won first prize for a picture that gives a look up and across the balloon field. In the image, a balloon in the shape of artist Vincent Van Gogh is seen floating. Just beyond is a balloon of Darth Vader from Star Wars and a balloon in the shape of a cow. They are among the many more traditional balloons in the sea-blue sky over the extraordinary Rio Grande Valley.
lines.zh: 在今年的摄影比赛中，杰夫·沃默凭一张仰望并横跨气球场的照片获得一等奖。照片中，一只画家文森特·梵高形状的气球飘浮着，远处是《星球大战》里达斯·维德形状的气球和一只奶牛形状的气球。它们和许多更传统的气球一起，飘在壮丽的格兰德河谷海蓝色的天空中。

lines.en: Balloon pilot Gary Michalek has been flying hot air balloons for 32 years and has been coming to the festival in Albuquerque for 20 years.
lines.zh: 热气球驾驶员加里·米哈莱克已经飞了 32 年热气球，来阿尔伯克基参加热气球节也有 20 年了。

lines.en: "Flying above the surface of the earth, like really close to the ground or high up, I mean, it's unique. You have few types of aviation where you can just float above the ground...."
lines.zh: “在地面上空飞行，不管是贴近地面还是飞得很高，我是说，那是独一无二的。能这样在地面上空飘浮的航空方式没几种……”

lines.en: Fiesta operations director Sam Parks is proud of his work. "One of the things that I heard yesterday, which really touched my heart, was a young boy telling his mother, 'This is the best day ever!'
lines.zh: 热气球节运营总监萨姆·帕克斯为自己的工作感到自豪。“昨天我听到的一件事真的打动了我：一个小男孩对他妈妈说，‘今天是最棒的一天！’”

lines.en: That, he added, "makes you feel like you're doing a good thing."
lines.zh: 他补充说，那“让你觉得自己在做一件好事”。

lines.en: I'm Ashley Thompson. And I'm Caty Weaver.
lines.zh: 我是阿什莉·汤普森。我是凯蒂·韦弗。

qs.q: Who were the first people to fly in a hot air balloon?
qs.why: "two Frenchmen were actually the first to float through the sky."

qs.q: Where is the biggest balloon festival in the world?
qs.why: "The biggest hot air balloon festival in the world takes place in... Albuquerque."

qs.q: What did Jonathan Trappe fly in 2014?
opts: a house like in the movie "Up"
qs.a: a house like in the movie "Up"
qs.why: "an airboat that looked much like the house in the 2009 film."

lessons.title: Central Park to Gain Statue of Women in History
lessons.zh: 纽约中央公园将立起历史女性雕像
lessons.sum: 纽约中央公园有 23 座历史男性人物的雕像，却没有一座真实女性的雕像，只有《爱丽丝梦游仙境》这类虚构人物。现在将新立一座雕像，纪念为女性选举权奋斗的三位领袖：苏珊·B·安东尼、伊丽莎白·卡迪·斯坦顿和索杰纳·特鲁斯。

lines.en: New York City will finally honor real women with a statue in its famous Central Park. City officials voted this week for the creation of a statue of three female civil rights leaders. Central Park has 23 statues of men who were important in history, but none of women.
lines.zh: 纽约市终于要在著名的中央公园里立一座雕像，纪念真实的女性了。市政官员本周投票决定，创作一座三位女性民权领袖的雕像。中央公园有 23 座历史上重要男性人物的雕像，却没有一座女性的。

lines.en: In fact, females are represented only by statues of imaginary characters. These include a statue of Alice, the hero of Alice in Wonderland books by 19th century British writer Lewis Carroll.
lines.zh: 事实上，公园里代表女性的只有虚构人物的雕像，其中包括爱丽丝——19 世纪英国作家刘易斯·卡罗尔的《爱丽丝梦游仙境》系列故事的主人公。

lines.en: The new statue from artist Meredith Bergmann is to be uncovered next August. Visitors will see the representation of past activists Susan B. Anthony, Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Sojourner Truth.
lines.zh: 艺术家梅雷迪思·伯格曼创作的新雕像将于明年 8 月揭幕。游客将看到过去的社会活动家苏珊·B·安东尼、伊丽莎白·卡迪·斯坦顿和索杰纳·特鲁斯的形象。

lines.en: The three women were contemporaries and leaders in the anti-slavery, women's rights and anti-alcohol movements. Their activism helped to secure the right of women to vote in 1920.
lines.zh: 这三位女性是同时代的人，是废除奴隶制、争取女性权利和禁酒运动的领袖。她们的努力帮助女性在 1920 年获得了选举权。

lines.en: Pam Elam is president of the non-profit organization Monumental Women. It worked with historians, community leaders and local officials in support of the statue. Elam said the artwork shows "the power of women working together to bring about revolutionary change in our society." The group privately raised $1.5 million to create and care for the new statue and a linked educational program.
lines.zh: 帕姆·埃拉姆是非营利组织“纪念碑女性”的主席。该组织与历史学家、社区领袖和地方官员合作，推动建立这座雕像。埃拉姆说，这件作品展示了“女性携手合作、给社会带来革命性变革的力量”。该组织私下募集了 150 万美元，用于创作和维护新雕像以及相关的教育项目。

lines.en: Bergmann's early design for the statue included only Anthony and Stanton. Observers criticized its lack of African-American representation, noting that women of that group were also important to the fight for women's suffrage. So, Bergmann redesigned the statue to add Truth.
lines.zh: 伯格曼最初的设计只有安东尼和斯坦顿。观察人士批评它缺少非裔美国人的代表，指出这个群体的女性在争取女性选举权的斗争中也很重要。所以伯格曼重新设计了雕像，加入了特鲁斯。

lines.en: Central Park is not the only area of New York limited in statues representing historical women. In fact, the government group She Built NYC says the large city of five boroughs has just five public statues of women from history.
lines.zh: 历史女性雕像少的不只是中央公园。事实上，政府团体“她建设了纽约”说，这座有五个行政区的大城市只有五座历史女性的公共雕像。

lines.en: A 2016 news story in the magazine Smithsonian.com reported that women were the subject of only about seven percent of public statues in the United States that depict real people.
lines.zh: Smithsonian.com 杂志 2016 年的一篇报道说，美国描绘真实人物的公共雕像中，只有约 7% 是女性。

lines.en: I'm Caty Weaver.
lines.zh: 我是凯蒂·韦弗。

qs.q: How many statues of real women did Central Park have before?
qs.why: "Central Park has 23 statues of men... but none of women."

qs.q: What did the three women help women win in 1920?
qs.why: "Their activism helped to secure the right of women to vote in 1920."

qs.q: Why did the artist add Sojourner Truth?
opts: People said the design lacked African-American representation.
The city asked for four women.
qs.a: People said the design lacked African-American representation.
qs.why: "Observers criticized its lack of African-American representation."

lessons.title: DC's Cherry Blossoms in Full Bloom
lessons.zh: 华盛顿的樱花盛开了
lessons.sum: 华盛顿潮汐湖畔的樱花进入盛花期。温暖的周末，本地人和游客在樱花树下野餐、拍照、划船。华盛顿的第一批樱花树是 1912 年东京市长赠送的，如今一年一度的樱花节庆祝美日之间的文化纽带。

lines.en: Washington, D.C.'s, cherry blossom trees are in full bloom.
lines.zh: 华盛顿的樱花树正值盛开。

lines.en: The United States National Park Service declared that the blossoms reached peak bloom on Monday. That means 70 percent of the Yoshino Cherry trees around the city's Tidal Basin are flowering. Depending on weather conditions, peak bloom can last between just a few days or seven to 10 days.
lines.zh: 美国国家公园管理局宣布，樱花在星期一达到盛花期。这意味着城里潮汐湖周围 70% 的染井吉野樱都开花了。根据天气情况，盛花期可能只持续几天，也可能持续七到十天。

lines.en: After what seemed like a long winter, mild weather returned to the DC area last weekend. On Saturday, the official daytime temperature reached 79 degrees Fahrenheit or 26 degrees Celsius. Many Washingtonians spent the day outdoors. They and thousands of out-of-town visitors walked among the cherry trees.
lines.zh: 在一个仿佛很漫长的冬天之后，上周末华盛顿地区回暖了。星期六，官方白天气温达到华氏 79 度，即摄氏 26 度。许多华盛顿人在户外度过了这一天。他们和数千名外地游客在樱花树下漫步。

lines.en: For a time, Washington did not feel like a busy capital city. The famous lack of political harmony was nowhere to be found. People smiled, laughed and pointed up at the tiny blossoms. Many lifted cell phones high in the air and took pictures. Families spread blankets on the grass and enjoyed picnics. Under a sunny sky, boaters drifted along the Potomac River. One could hear people speaking in different languages, including Japanese, Chinese, German and Spanish.
lines.zh: 有那么一段时间，华盛顿感觉不像一座繁忙的首都。出了名的政治不和谐在这里一点也看不到。人们笑着，指着头顶上小小的樱花。很多人把手机高高举起拍照。一家家人在草地上铺开毯子野餐。阳光下，游船在波托马克河上漂荡。你能听到人们说着不同的语言，包括日语、汉语、德语和西班牙语。

lines.en: Sitting near the water, Leanna Gonzalez of Washington wore a dazzling cherry blossom colored gown. Her mother, Maria, paid a photographer to take pictures of the 15-year-old to mark her quinceañera, a coming of age ceremony for Hispanic girls.
lines.zh: 华盛顿的莉安娜·冈萨雷斯坐在水边，穿着一件耀眼的樱花色礼服。她的妈妈玛丽亚请了一位摄影师给这个 15 岁的女孩拍照，纪念她的“成人礼”（quinceañera）——拉美裔女孩的成年仪式。

lines.en: "She looks like a princess," her mother said, smiling.
lines.zh: “她看起来像个公主。”她妈妈笑着说。

lines.en: Jack Elmira and his twin 10-year-old sons, Toby and Joe, walked among the trees, looking up into the blossoms. They had planned to visit Washington for more than a year and were pleased that they had timed their trip correctly.
lines.zh: 杰克·埃尔米拉和他 10 岁的双胞胎儿子托比和乔在树下散步，仰头看着樱花。他们计划来华盛顿已经一年多了，很高兴把时间掐得正好。

lines.en: "I was here once before," Jack Elmira said, "but the trees still had frost on them. That was years ago. I'm just happy my sons get to see them at their best."
lines.zh: “我以前来过一次，”杰克·埃尔米拉说，“可那时树上还有霜。那是好多年前了。我很高兴儿子们能看到樱花最美的时候。”

lines.en: DC's first cherry trees were a gift from Tokyo Mayor Yukio Ozaki back in 1912. Today, the cherry blossom festival takes place every year. It celebrates the close cultural ties between the United States and Japan. The Park Service said it expects more than 1.5 million people to walk among the more than 3,000 white and pink trees over the next few days.
lines.zh: 华盛顿的第一批樱花树是东京市长尾崎行雄在 1912 年赠送的。如今，樱花节每年举行，庆祝美日之间密切的文化联系。公园管理局说，预计未来几天会有 150 多万人在 3000 多棵白色和粉色的樱花树间漫步。

lines.en: Some people also walked across the National Mall to the World War II Memorial. It was built in 2004 to honor the 16 million Americans who fought in the war. Its fountains throw off cool drops of water with the Washington Monument in the background.
lines.zh: 有些人还穿过国家广场，去了二战纪念碑。它建于 2004 年，纪念参战的 1600 万美国人。纪念碑的喷泉溅起清凉的水珠，背后是华盛顿纪念碑。

lines.en: Visitors can place their feet in the water or take pictures at its edge. Lucy Manor of Arlington, Virginia, carefully walked along the edge.
lines.zh: 游客可以把脚伸进水里，或者在水边拍照。弗吉尼亚州阿灵顿的露西·马诺小心翼翼地沿着池边走着。

lines.en: "These are the days when Washington feels like a dream city," she said.
lines.zh: “在这样的日子里，华盛顿感觉就像一座梦想之城。”她说。

lines.en: The National Cherry Blossom Festival continues until Saturday, April 13, and ends with the festival's parade. The parade march stretches along Constitution Avenue and is open to the public.
lines.zh: 全国樱花节一直持续到 4 月 13 日星期六，以樱花节游行结束。游行队伍沿宪法大道行进，对公众开放。

lines.en: I'm Susan Shand.
lines.zh: 我是苏珊·尚德。

qs.q: What does "peak bloom" mean here?
opts: 70 percent of the trees are flowering
qs.a: 70 percent of the trees are flowering
qs.why: "That means 70 percent of the Yoshino Cherry trees... are flowering."

qs.q: Who gave DC its first cherry trees?
qs.why: "a gift from Tokyo Mayor Yukio Ozaki back in 1912."

qs.q: What is a quinceañera?
opts: a coming of age ceremony for Hispanic girls
qs.a: a coming of age ceremony for Hispanic girls
qs.why: "a coming of age ceremony for Hispanic girls."

lessons.title: What an American Home Looks Like
lessons.zh: 美国人的房子长什么样
lessons.sum: 美国的房子就像美国本身，融合了多国风格：殖民地式的方盒子小楼、色彩缤纷的维多利亚式房子、镀金时代富豪的豪宅、西尔斯邮购的成套组装房、赖特设计的低矮“草原式”住宅，还有被戏称为“麦当劳豪宅”的大房子。

lines.en: American homes are a lot like America. They are a mix of designs from many countries, all combined together.
lines.zh: 美国人的房子很像美国，是许多国家的设计融合在一起的混合体。

lines.en: For example, a visitor to a neighborhood in the United States might see several kinds of colonial houses. Workers began building these houses in the 1600s, when Britain ruled the area.
lines.zh: 比如，到美国某个街区的游客可能会看到好几种殖民地式房子。工人们从 17 世纪英国统治这一地区时就开始建这种房子了。

lines.en: Colonial houses are often box-shaped, two-story houses. They have a front door in the middle, and five or seven windows. Both sides of the house are usually the same.
lines.zh: 殖民地式房子通常是方盒子形状的两层楼房，正门在中间，有五扇或七扇窗户，房子两边通常是对称的。

lines.en: Their original design came from ancient Roman and Greek buildings. But over time, Americans added design elements from the architectural styles of other countries.
lines.zh: 它们最初的设计来自古罗马和古希腊的建筑。但随着时间推移，美国人加入了其他国家建筑风格的设计元素。

lines.en: One modern-day colonial home can have a tall French-style roof, like the Louvre museum in Paris. Another can have narrow Greek columns near the front door, like the U.S. White House. Another can have long pieces of wood on the outside, like some houses in England during the Middle Ages. Or the same house can have all three!
lines.zh: 一栋现代殖民地式房子可能有一个像巴黎卢浮宫那样高高的法式屋顶；另一栋可能在正门附近有细长的希腊式柱子，像美国白宫那样；还有一栋外墙可能有长长的木条，像中世纪英格兰的一些房子；或者同一栋房子三样都有！

lines.en: Jackie Craven is a reporter who writes about architecture. She told VOA over email, "Our homes, like our people, draw from many sources."
lines.zh: 杰基·克雷文是一位撰写建筑报道的记者。她通过电子邮件告诉 VOA：“我们的房子，就像我们的人一样，有着多种来源。”

lines.en: The style of American homes also show what was happening in the country at the time they were built. In the 1800s, the U.S. was growing economically. Workers learned how to make many copies of the same thing quickly, for not very much money. One result is that a number of Americans could pay for the building of large, complex houses. These are called Victorians after Queen Victoria who ruled Britain from 1837 to 1901.
lines.zh: 美国房子的风格也反映了建造时国家正在发生的事。19 世纪，美国经济不断增长。工人们学会了快速、廉价地大量复制同一样东西。结果之一是，不少美国人有钱建造又大又复杂的房子。这些房子以 1837 年到 1901 年统治英国的维多利亚女王命名，叫“维多利亚式”。

lines.en: Victorian houses follow Queen Victoria's romantic image. They are usually three stories tall and asymmetrical – in other words, the sides are not the same in size or shape. One side may have large windows. Another may have a porch. One side might also be tall and rounded. Victorians also have detailed wood cutouts for visual appeal.
lines.zh: 维多利亚式房子追随着维多利亚女王的浪漫形象。它们通常有三层高，不对称——也就是说两边的大小和形状不一样。一边可能有大窗户，另一边可能有门廊，还有一边可能又高又圆。维多利亚式房子还有精细的木雕镂空装饰，十分好看。

lines.en: At first, Victorians were painted in a mix of earthy colors, like browns, greens and dark orange. In later years bright pinks, blues and yellows became popular combinations.
lines.zh: 起初，维多利亚式房子漆成褐色、绿色、深橙色这类大地色系的组合。后来，亮粉、亮蓝和亮黄的搭配流行起来。

lines.en: Some observers compare Victorian houses to doll houses, gingerbread houses or even wedding cakes.
lines.zh: 有些人把维多利亚式房子比作玩偶屋、姜饼屋，甚至婚礼蛋糕。

lines.en: They look fancy, but they are modest in relation to some houses that came later.
lines.zh: 它们看上去很花哨，但和后来的一些房子比起来还算朴素。

lines.en: At the end of the 1800s, the Industrial Revolution made steel part of the American environment. Steel helped build railroads and skyscrapers.
lines.zh: 19 世纪末，工业革命让钢铁成为美国环境的一部分。钢铁帮助修建了铁路和摩天大楼。

lines.en: It also helped make a few American businessmen very wealthy. Some built extremely large mansions that looked more like European castles than family homes.
lines.zh: 它也让少数美国商人变得非常富有。有些人建造了极其巨大的豪宅，看上去更像欧洲城堡，而不像家庭住宅。

lines.en: They mixed old Italian, French, and Roman Empire building traditions that aimed to show how powerful and rich the owners were. Inside, the mansions had huge stairways and dining rooms big enough for 100 people.
lines.zh: 这些豪宅混合了古意大利、法国和罗马帝国的建筑传统，目的是显示主人有多么有权有钱。里面有巨大的楼梯，还有能容纳 100 人的餐厅。

lines.en: But by the beginning of the 1900s, some people were rejecting shows of wealth by powerful people. And many Americans needed housing that was far less costly, especially during the economic depression of the 1930s.
lines.zh: 可是到了 20 世纪初，一些人开始反感有权势的人炫耀财富。许多美国人需要便宜得多的住房，特别是在 20 世纪 30 年代的经济大萧条期间。

lines.en: So houses became simpler and smaller. One company, called Sears, made house building kits you could order from a catalogue. The business sent you the parts and the plans for the house. Then you and a few friends built it yourself. The houses lasted, too – about 70 percent of Sears kit houses are still standing.
lines.zh: 于是房子变得更简单、更小了。一家叫西尔斯的公司推出了可以从商品目录上订购的盖房套件。公司把房子的零件和图纸寄给你，然后你和几个朋友自己动手盖。这些房子也很耐用——大约 70% 的西尔斯套件房至今仍然屹立。

lines.en: During the same years that Sears was mailing housing kits, an architect named Frank Lloyd Wright was creating a new kind of American house.
lines.zh: 就在西尔斯邮寄盖房套件的那些年，一位名叫弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特的建筑师正在创造一种新的美国房子。

lines.en: Wright did not want to use European ideas. He believed American houses should fit into the nature around them. Some of his most famous houses are long and low, with clean lines and a simple style. The roof hangs far over and beyond the walls, so the area outside feels more connected to the structure. Inside, the rooms are all connected.
lines.zh: 赖特不想用欧洲的理念。他认为美国的房子应该融入周围的自然。他最有名的一些房子又长又矮，线条简洁，风格朴素。屋顶远远伸出墙外，让屋外的空间和建筑感觉更紧密。屋里的房间都是相通的。

lines.en: Wright designed more than 1,000 houses in his life. His influence can be seen in a huge number of American homes built in the 20th century. They are especially common in neighborhoods just outside of cities, called suburbs. For example, the ranch house on the 1960s and 70s television show "The Brady Bunch" was influenced by Frank Lloyd Wright.
lines.zh: 赖特一生设计了 1000 多栋房子。在 20 世纪建造的大量美国住宅中都能看到他的影响，尤其是在城市边缘叫作“郊区”的社区里。比如，20 世纪六七十年代电视剧《脱线家族》里的牧场式房子，就受到了赖特的影响。

lines.en: Susan Piedmont-Palladino is an architect and the director of Virginia Tech's Washington Alexandria Architecture Center. She calls the history of American homes an "all-you-can-eat buffet." In other words, Americans have many home styles to choose from.
lines.zh: 苏珊·皮埃蒙特-帕拉迪诺是一位建筑师，也是弗吉尼亚理工大学华盛顿-亚历山德里亚建筑中心的主任。她把美国住宅的历史称为“自助餐”——也就是说，美国人有很多房屋风格可以选择。

lines.en: "We can borrow anybody's style of architecture, and I'm not sure that's the attitude in other countries around the world," she says.
lines.zh: “我们可以借用任何人的建筑风格，我不确定世界上其他国家是不是也这样。”她说。

lines.en: And Piedmont-Palladino says American homes are different in another way. She observes that most American homes are for just one family: one set of parents and their children. The single family house, she says, "dominates" American neighborhoods.
lines.zh: 皮埃蒙特-帕拉迪诺说，美国的房子还有一点不同。她发现大多数美国房子只住一个家庭：一对父母和他们的孩子。她说，独栋住宅在美国社区中“占主导地位”。

lines.en: She also notes that as American families are getting smaller, American houses are getting bigger. For example, in the late 1900s some Americans built large houses again to show their wealth and power.
lines.zh: 她还指出，美国家庭越来越小，美国的房子却越来越大。比如在 20 世纪后期，一些美国人又建起大房子来显示自己的财富和权势。

lines.en: But these houses are not as unique or beautiful as the mansions of the late 1800s. Many of them look similar to each other. They are known in a negative way as McMansions – mansions that are as common and quickly made as the food at a McDonalds fast food restaurant.
lines.zh: 但这些房子没有 19 世纪末的豪宅那么独特、那么美。很多房子看起来都差不多。它们被贬称为“麦当劳豪宅”（McMansion）——像麦当劳快餐一样普通、做得一样快的豪宅。

lines.en: Piedmont-Palladino says in the future, she would like to see American houses move a different direction. She hopes owners and builders will seek designs that are friendly to the environment and use resources wisely.
lines.zh: 皮埃蒙特-帕拉迪诺说，她希望将来美国的房子朝不同的方向发展。她希望房主和建筑商寻求对环境友好、明智利用资源的设计。

lines.en: I'm Kelly Jean Kelly.
lines.zh: 我是凯莉·琼·凯莉。

qs.q: What does a colonial house usually look like?
opts: a box-shaped two-story house with a door in the middle
qs.a: a box-shaped two-story house with a door in the middle
qs.why: "Colonial houses are often box-shaped, two-story houses."

qs.q: What could you order from the Sears catalogue?
qs.why: "made house building kits you could order from a catalogue."

qs.q: What is a "McMansion"?
opts: a large house that looks like many others
qs.a: a large house that looks like many others
qs.why: "mansions that are as common and quickly made as the food at a McDonalds."

lessons.title: Man Builds His Dream House (A Very Small One)
lessons.zh: 他造了一座梦想之家（很小的那种）
lessons.sum: 洛杉矶设计师克里斯·托莱多住在两居室公寓里，却花两年时间亲手造了一座西班牙风格的微缩豪宅：手绘 6000 多块地砖、自制灯具，连水槽上的水渍和蜘蛛网都做了出来。有人出价 8 万美元想买下它。

lines.en: Many of us think about our dream home.
lines.zh: 我们很多人都会想象自己的梦想之家。

lines.en: When designer Chris Toledo dreams about his, he lets his imagination run wild. He wants a Spanish-style house with hand-painted floor tiles, circling staircases and at least 12 bedrooms.
lines.zh: 设计师克里斯·托莱多想象他的梦想之家时，会让想象力尽情驰骋。他想要一栋西班牙风格的房子，有手绘地砖、旋转楼梯，至少 12 间卧室。

lines.en: That is his dream.
lines.zh: 那是他的梦想。

lines.en: For now, Toledo lives in a small, two-bedroom apartment. But that has not stopped him from building his dream home. It is just a lot…smaller. A lot.
lines.zh: 目前，托莱多住在一套小小的两居室公寓里。但这并没有阻止他建造自己的梦想之家，只是它要……小得多。小很多很多。

lines.en: Toledo was born and raised in southern California. He has been working on his miniature Spanish-style dream home for the past two years.
lines.zh: 托莱多在南加州出生长大。过去两年里，他一直在打造他的西班牙风格微缩梦想之家。

lines.en: "Here in California Spanish-style that's very common. You can't go anywhere in Los Angeles without seeing Spanish-style houses."
lines.zh: “在加州这里，西班牙风格非常常见。在洛杉矶走到哪儿都能看到西班牙风格的房子。”

lines.en: The beauty of these mansions is there for anyone to see -- on the outside. But it is not easy to get a look at the inside of these homes. Homeowners protect their mansions with security gates, walls and in some cases armed guards.
lines.zh: 这些豪宅的美，任何人都能看到——从外面看。可要看到这些房子的内部可不容易。房主们用安全门、围墙保护自己的豪宅，有的还有持枪警卫。

lines.en: But Toledo found a way to get around all that security. He went online and looked at houses for sale on real estate websites.
lines.zh: 但托莱多找到了绕过这些安保的办法。他上网在房地产网站上看待售的房子。

lines.en: "I would go on real estate websites and look at houses there for sale that are the same style, the same age period. I would just look for all the original details. And most of the houses that I used for inspiration…they were probably about $2 to $10 million dollars."
lines.zh: “我会上房地产网站，看那些风格相同、年代相同的待售房子，专门找所有原有的细节。我用来找灵感的大部分房子……大概价值 200 万到 1000 万美元。”

lines.en: Inspired by the Mediterranean style, he researched this style thoroughly. He filled his Spanish-style mini-mansion with objects true to that style – many he made by hand.
lines.zh: 受地中海风格启发，他对这种风格做了彻底的研究。他在这座西班牙风格的迷你豪宅里摆满了忠于这种风格的物品——很多是他亲手做的。

lines.en: His miniature version is as real as he can make it. His small house is made of real wood. He covered the wood with a material that would have been part of a real Spanish-style of building. He hand-painted over 6,000 small tiles for the floors.
lines.zh: 他的微缩版尽可能做得逼真。小房子用真木头做成，他在木头上涂了真正西班牙风格建筑会用的材料。他亲手绘制了 6000 多块小地砖。

lines.en: The house even has electricity; Toledo made all the lights by hand. He also made many other household objects, like tables and pillows. Other objects he bought and then painted them to fit the house. He even included a copy of a very old oil painting that he found in a book on Spanish design.
lines.zh: 房子里甚至通了电；所有的灯都是托莱多亲手做的。他还做了很多别的家居用品，比如桌子和枕头。其他东西是买来再涂色，让它们和房子相配。他甚至放了一幅很古老的油画的复制品，是他在一本西班牙设计的书里找到的。

lines.en: Toledo's final creation is extremely true-to-life. The bathroom sinks have water markings. The lighting fixtures have extremely small spider webs. Other pieces have dust on them.
lines.zh: 托莱多最后的作品极其逼真：浴室水槽上有水渍，灯具上挂着极小的蜘蛛网，其他物件上还落着灰尘。

lines.en: The only thing his miniature mansion does not have is running water; Toledo was afraid it would ruin the building.
lines.zh: 他的微缩豪宅唯一没有的就是自来水；托莱多怕水会毁了这座建筑。

lines.en: One person has already offered Toledo $80,000 for his miniature dream home. Toledo says he plans to use that money for a down payment on a home. It may not be a mansion but it will be real…and full-sized.
lines.zh: 已经有人出价 8 万美元想买托莱多的微缩梦想之家。托莱多说，他打算用这笔钱付一套房子的首付。那也许不是豪宅，但会是真的……而且是正常大小的。

lines.en: I'm Anna Matteo.
lines.zh: 我是安娜·马泰奥。

qs.q: How did Toledo see inside Spanish-style mansions?
qs.why: "He went online and looked at houses for sale on real estate websites."

qs.q: How many tiles did he paint by hand?
qs.why: "He hand-painted over 6,000 small tiles for the floors."

qs.q: What will he do with the $80,000?
opts: make a down payment on a real home
qs.a: make a down payment on a real home
qs.why: "he plans to use that money for a down payment on a home."

lessons.title: Maps Provide a Special View of American History
lessons.zh: 地图里的美国历史
lessons.sum: 历史学家舒尔滕在《100 幅地图里的美国史》中，用地图讲述普通人的希望与恐惧：19 世纪初女学生画的精美地图、切罗基人眼中的部落力量、反映华人遭受歧视的旧金山唐人街地图，以及推动禁酒、废奴和女性选举权的地图。

lines.en: When people use maps, they are usually seeking directions to a place they want to go.
lines.zh: 人们用地图时，通常是想找去某个地方的路线。

lines.en: But Susan Schulten sees much more in maps, like history, culture and art. She shares some of those findings in her book, A History of America in 100 Maps.
lines.zh: 可苏珊·舒尔滕在地图里看到的远不止这些，还有历史、文化和艺术。她在《100 幅地图里的美国史》一书中分享了其中一些发现。

lines.en: Schulten travels back in time, using maps of the past. Her book explores the hopes, dreams and fears of ordinary people dating back to before the United States came to be.
lines.zh: 舒尔滕借助过去的地图回到从前。她的书探讨了普通人的希望、梦想和恐惧，一直追溯到美国建国之前。

lines.en: "There is practically no area of American history where maps don't sort of enrich our understanding," Schulten said. "Maps record past scenarios, past situations, past relationships of power, but they also influenced people at the time in terms of future decision making."
lines.zh: “美国历史上几乎没有哪个领域，地图不能丰富我们的理解，”舒尔滕说，“地图记录了过去的情景、过去的处境、过去的权力关系，但它们也在当时影响了人们对未来的决策。”

lines.en: Schulten is a history professor at the University of Denver, in Colorado. She studies cartography, the making of maps. During her research, she became very interested in a series of maps made by American schoolgirls in the early 1800s. The detailed maps appealed to her not only for their beauty, but also because of what they taught about a little-known period in American education.
lines.zh: 舒尔滕是科罗拉多州丹佛大学的历史学教授，研究地图学，也就是地图的绘制。研究过程中，她对 19 世纪初美国女学生绘制的一系列地图产生了浓厚兴趣。这些精细的地图吸引她，不仅因为美，还因为它们揭示了美国教育史上一段鲜为人知的时期。

lines.en: "New schools educating young women for the first time outside the home prepared a curriculum that involved teaching them not just geography but map drawing," she says. She says the girls studied technical methods of art, writing and understanding geography by creating their own maps.
lines.zh: “第一次在家庭以外教育年轻女性的新学校，制定了一套课程，不仅教她们地理，还教她们画地图。”她说。她说，女孩们通过绘制自己的地图，学习艺术技法、写作和对地理的理解。

lines.en: The schools for girls were open for only a short time. Knowledge of them might have been lost if not for the maps they left behind.
lines.zh: 这些女子学校只开办了很短时间。要不是她们留下的地图，关于这些学校的知识可能早就失传了。

lines.en: Schulten says those early maps also helped establish a national identity and loyalty for the United States in its early days.
lines.zh: 舒尔滕说，这些早期地图也帮助美国在建国初期确立了国家认同和忠诚。

lines.en: Schulten says that most American colonists were first loyal to their colony and then to the King of England. After independence, schools became a place to establish a shared meaning of the new country.
lines.zh: 舒尔滕说，大多数美国殖民者首先忠于自己的殖民地，然后才是英国国王。独立之后，学校成了建立对这个新国家共同理解的地方。

lines.en: "There's such an emphasis after the Revolution on using education to help create a civic identity and it becomes readily apparent," Schulten says.
lines.zh: “独立战争之后，人们非常重视用教育来帮助塑造公民身份，这一点很明显。”舒尔滕说。

lines.en: The book also includes some Native American maps. They help shape an understanding of how Natives saw power relationships. A 1721 map, most likely made by a Cherokee leader, includes a number of circles. The sizes of the circles are linked to the perceived power of the individual tribes.
lines.zh: 书中还收录了一些美洲原住民的地图，帮助人们理解原住民如何看待权力关系。一幅很可能由切罗基部落首领绘制的 1721 年地图上有许多圆圈，圆圈的大小与各部落被认为的力量大小相关。

lines.en: "It's a representation of space from a non-European perspective," Schulten said.
lines.zh: “这是从非欧洲视角来表现空间。”舒尔滕说。

lines.en: Some maps in the book recall dark moments in American history.
lines.zh: 书中有些地图让人想起美国历史上的黑暗时刻。

lines.en: An 1885 report on the Chinatown neighborhood in San Francisco, California, helps tell of the racism that Chinese laborers experienced. These immigrants had helped build the transcontinental railroad. After it was complete, many of the workers settled in San Francisco.
lines.zh: 一份 1885 年关于加州旧金山唐人街的报告，讲述了华人劳工遭受的种族歧视。这些移民曾帮助修建横贯大陆的铁路。铁路建成后，许多工人在旧金山定居。

lines.en: A report commissioned by city supervisors described the Chinese in extremely offensive race-based terms. A map made for the report shows opium places, gambling establishments and houses where sex was sold in Chinatown.
lines.zh: 这份由市议员委托撰写的报告，用极其冒犯的种族主义言辞描述华人。为报告绘制的一幅地图，标出了唐人街的鸦片馆、赌场和卖淫场所。

lines.en: The message of the report and map was that the Chinese should be removed.
lines.zh: 这份报告和地图传达的信息是：华人应该被赶走。

lines.en: From political moves like gerrymandering, to advertising, to "red" and "blue" states, maps tell many American stories. They can also be used to push reform, and help to set the country on a new course.
lines.zh: 从“操纵选区划分”这样的政治手段，到广告，再到“红州”和“蓝州”，地图讲述了许多美国故事。它们也可以被用来推动改革，帮助国家走上新的道路。

lines.en: Schulten says there were maps used to support the anti-alcohol movement, the opposition to slavery and the fight gain voting rights for women.
lines.zh: 舒尔滕说，有些地图曾被用来支持禁酒运动、反对奴隶制以及争取女性选举权的斗争。

lines.en: A History of America in 100 Maps includes maps never before published, Schulten said. Others are well known. But all can provide a special understanding of America's past.
lines.zh: 舒尔滕说，《100 幅地图里的美国史》收录了一些从未发表过的地图，其他的则很有名。但它们都能让人对美国的过去有一种特别的理解。

lines.en: I'm Caty Weaver.
lines.zh: 我是凯蒂·韦弗。

qs.q: What did schoolgirls in the early 1800s learn?
qs.why: "teaching them not just geography but map drawing."

qs.q: What did the circles on the 1721 Cherokee map show?
qs.why: "The sizes of the circles are linked to the perceived power of the individual tribes."

qs.q: What did the 1885 San Francisco map show?
qs.why: "helps tell of the racism that Chinese laborers experienced."

gloss: （为政党利益）不公正地划分选区

lessons.title: Building a Truly American Instrument
lessons.zh: 制作一件地道的美国乐器：班卓琴
lessons.sum: 班卓琴是美国南方蓝草音乐的灵魂。它由非洲奴隶带到美国，后被南方人用来创造乡村音乐。田纳西州的汤姆·乔治自学成才，和徒弟克里斯蒂安·斯坦菲尔德全部手工制琴，做一把要四到六个月。

lines.en: Parts of the south in the United States are known for a kind of country music called bluegrass. And there is one instrument that is an important part of the bluegrass sound.
lines.zh: 美国南方部分地区以一种叫“蓝草”的乡村音乐闻名。有一种乐器是蓝草音乐的重要组成部分。

lines.en: The banjo is a truly American instrument. It was brought to the United States by African slaves and then was adopted by people of the south to create their country music.
lines.zh: 班卓琴是一件地道的美国乐器。它由非洲奴隶带到美国，后来被南方人用来创作他们的乡村音乐。

lines.en: "Really, the banjo is the American instrument and it was made by both black and white cultures [that] came together to produce this instrument."
lines.zh: “说真的，班卓琴就是美国的乐器，它是黑人文化和白人文化相遇、共同创造出来的乐器。”

lines.en: That is Christian Stanfield. He and his teacher, Tom George, have made the complex art of banjo making their lifetime project.
lines.zh: 说这话的是克里斯蒂安·斯坦菲尔德。他和他的老师汤姆·乔治把复杂的班卓琴制作工艺当成了一生的事业。

lines.en: It began decades ago when Stanfield moved from Washington, D.C. to Memphis, Tennessee. He went to a dance party that featured folk music and the banjo. He says as soon as he heard the banjo, he fell in love. He borrowed one from a banjo player and got some good advice on where to buy one.
lines.zh: 这要从几十年前斯坦菲尔德从华盛顿搬到田纳西州孟菲斯说起。他去参加了一个有民间音乐和班卓琴演奏的舞会。他说，一听到班卓琴，他就爱上了它。他向一位班卓琴手借了一把琴，还得到了去哪儿买琴的好建议。

lines.en: "I fell in love with the banjo, I really wanted to learn that new instrument. So I borrowed a banjo from him for two or three months and when I was ready to get a banjo of my own, he recommended Tommy to me. He said, you know, don't buy a banjo on the Internet or in the store. There's a guy in Fayette County, [Tennessee] who builds them!"
lines.zh: “我爱上了班卓琴，真的很想学这件新乐器。所以我向他借了两三个月的班卓琴。等我准备买一把自己的琴时，他把汤米推荐给了我。他说，你知道，别在网上或店里买班卓琴。（田纳西州）费耶特县有个人会做琴！”

lines.en: That man was Tom George -- one of the best-known banjo makers in the U.S.
lines.zh: 那个人就是汤姆·乔治——美国最有名的班卓琴制作者之一。

lines.en: "I just like to make things -- woodwork and banjos, furniture … whatever!"
lines.zh: “我就是喜欢做东西——木工活、班卓琴、家具……什么都行！”

lines.en: Tom George knows a true banjo-lover when he sees one. So, when Stanfield asked to become his student, George quickly agreed. He taught Stanfield his banjo-making secrets … after dinner, of course!
lines.zh: 汤姆·乔治一眼就能认出真正热爱班卓琴的人。所以斯坦菲尔德请求拜他为师时，乔治很快就答应了。他把制作班卓琴的秘诀教给了斯坦菲尔德……当然是在晚饭后！

lines.en: "I would come over and his wife would cook dinner. And we would eat dinner and then we would go out in the shop and work for a couple of hours. And in three months I had a banjo that I had made myself."
lines.zh: “我会去他家，他妻子做晚饭。我们吃完晚饭，就去作坊干两个小时活。三个月后，我就有了一把自己亲手做的班卓琴。”

lines.en: Tom George, however, did not have a teacher. He taught himself how to build banjos.
lines.zh: 不过汤姆·乔治没有老师，他是自学怎么做班卓琴的。

lines.en: "I wanted a banjo when I was a teenager, so I mowed yards around my neighborhood to raise money and I bought a banjo. The one that I bought, which wasn't very good, and I said maybe I can improve it, so I started trying to improve that one… "
lines.zh: “我十几岁时想要一把班卓琴，就在附近给人家割草攒钱，买了一把。我买的那把不怎么好，我就想，也许我能把它改好，于是就开始试着改……”

lines.en: Today, George and Stanfield have a banjo-making workshop, an hour's drive from Memphis, Tennessee. Visitors can tour their shop and see the hundreds of small parts that all come together to make the finished banjo. The two men make everything by hand. So, it is not surprising that it takes around 4 to 6 months to make one banjo.
lines.zh: 如今，乔治和斯坦菲尔德有一个班卓琴作坊，离田纳西州孟菲斯一小时车程。游客可以参观作坊，看到组成一把成品班卓琴的几百个小零件。两人全部手工制作，所以做一把班卓琴要花四到六个月也就不奇怪了。

lines.en: The banjo has two distinct parts: the round part and the straight part.
lines.zh: 班卓琴有两个截然不同的部分：圆的部分和直的部分。

lines.en: "There are two distinct parts. There's the round part and you have the straight part. And they're made separately."
lines.zh: “有两个截然不同的部分：圆的部分和直的部分。它们是分开做的。”

lines.en: The round part -- the body of the banjo -- is made of wood bent around a form to give the instrument its round shape.
lines.zh: 圆的部分——琴身——是把木头绕着模具弯曲，让乐器有圆形的外观。

lines.en: Stanfield explains that part of the process.
lines.zh: 斯坦菲尔德解释了这道工序。

lines.en: "I will re-saw it into smaller pieces like this. And I'll put it in a steam box and the steam will make it very soft. And then I will put it in this form and it will actually be able to bend without breaking, it'll bend around this …"
lines.zh: “我会把木头再锯成这样的小块，放进蒸箱里，蒸汽会让它变得很软。然后我把它放进这个模具，它就能弯曲而不会断，绕着这个弯过来……”

lines.en: After the banjo is finished, Tom George carefully wipes it clean. It is ready to be played. And then the team can do the other thing they love to do -- play the banjo.
lines.zh: 班卓琴做好后，汤姆·乔治小心地把它擦干净，就可以弹了。接下来，两人就可以做他们喜欢的另一件事——弹班卓琴。

qs.q: Who first brought the banjo to the United States?
qs.why: "It was brought to the United States by African slaves."

qs.q: How did Tom George learn to make banjos?
qs.why: "He taught himself how to build banjos."

qs.q: How long does it take to make one banjo?
qs.why: "it takes around 4 to 6 months to make one banjo."

lessons.title: New Statue of Liberty Museum Honors the Immigrant Experience
lessons.zh: 新的自由女神像博物馆致敬移民经历
lessons.sum: 1892 年到 1954 年间，1200 多万移民乘船经过自由女神像前往埃利斯岛。自由岛上的新博物馆让每位游客都能“看到”雕像内部，还展出了照亮纽约港近百年的原火炬。

lines.en: A new 2,400 square-meter museum is set to open on New York State's Liberty Island next year.
lines.zh: 一座 2400 平方米的新博物馆将于明年在纽约州的自由岛开放。

lines.en: The museum celebrates the world famous Statue of Liberty. The statue was a gift from the people of France to the United States. It officially opened to the public in October 1886.
lines.zh: 这座博物馆是为闻名世界的自由女神像而建的。自由女神像是法国人民送给美国的礼物，于 1886 年 10 月正式对公众开放。

lines.en: From 1892 to 1954, more than 12 million immigrants passed by the Statue of Liberty as their ships sailed to nearby Ellis Island. Many immigrants later traveled to Liberty Island and saw the statue up close. At the bottom, are the words of poet Emma Lazarus: "Give me your tired, your poor, your huddled masses yearning to breathe free…"
lines.zh: 1892 年到 1954 年间，1200 多万移民乘船前往附近的埃利斯岛时，都从自由女神像旁经过。许多移民后来去了自由岛，近距离看到了雕像。雕像底座上刻着诗人埃玛·拉扎勒斯的诗句：“把你们疲惫的人、贫穷的人、渴望呼吸自由的蜷缩的人群交给我……”

lines.en: Now, a new museum to honor 'Lady Liberty' is on the way.
lines.zh: 现在，一座纪念“自由女神”的新博物馆即将建成。

lines.en: Nicholas Garrison is a partner with FXCollaborative, a New York-based company that plans and designs buildings. He designed the museum.
lines.zh: 尼古拉斯·加里森是纽约一家规划和设计建筑的公司 FXCollaborative 的合伙人，他设计了这座博物馆。

lines.en: "When we first came on the island, we were moved. We…saw people on their knees, crying, because of what this place meant, and it kind of sunk into us that this is a really special, sacred place."
lines.zh: “我们第一次来到岛上时很受触动。我们……看到有人跪在地上哭，因为这个地方对他们意义重大。我们渐渐体会到，这是一个非常特别、神圣的地方。”

lines.en: About 4.5 million tourists visit Liberty Island every year. But only about 20 percent are able to go inside the Statue of Liberty because of limited space. The new museum will permit every visitor to know what the inside is like.
lines.zh: 每年约有 450 万游客来自由岛，但由于空间有限，只有约 20% 的人能进入自由女神像内部。新博物馆将让每位游客都了解雕像内部是什么样子。

lines.en: The museum is expected to open in May 2019.
lines.zh: 博物馆预计于 2019 年 5 月开放。

lines.en: Entering the building, visitors will experience a virtual look inside the head of Lady Liberty. They also have a chance to see a recreation of the work place of Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi, who created the statue.
